liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Wheel** (2 reviews): Reviewer highlights the transition from The Wheel to Never Trust A Woman; Extended jam in second set cited as probably the best of the 80s [11][19]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer loves the first set closer transition to I Know You Rider [18]
- **Never Trust A Woman** (1 review): First performance noted, followed by an extended Jerry, Brent, and Rhythm Devils jam [19]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): Jam based on a two-chord vamp from Miles Davis' Sketches From Spain [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-08-28.mtx.painoman.92893.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 174 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1981-08-28.153337.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1981-08-28.fob.ellner.motb.91231.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 180 min; rated 4.11/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Recording features high energy, strong interplay, and occasional track slipping [9]
- **gd1981-08-28.sbd.miller.113680.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 182 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: Spanish Jam described as heart-wrenching and placing listeners into a catatonic flip [20]
- **gd1981-08-28.149185.FOB.Senn.Streeter.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac2496**: source not stated; 22 songs; 180 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [6]

## Around the show

- Dan Healy's onstage mix praised for remarkable skills and sync [14]
- Matrix considered a definitive upgrade over previous SBD and MOTB choices [11]
- Audience recording deemed as good as the flawless soundboard [14]
- Matrix sound clearly blows away the available soundboard recording [16]
- Paired with the 27th, forms one of the finest 80s runs [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-08-28.mtx.painoman.92893.sbeok.flac16**: Encore source identified as Ron Ellner's master, not Barry Glassberg's [12]
- **gd1981-08-28.153337.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 304 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [2]. Also: Jim Vita provided master; Charlie Miller transferred; Sennheiser 421 patched Never Trust A Woman; Todd Ellner and MOTB provided Nakamichi 700 source for Drums and Truckin' patches [2]
- **gd1981-08-28.fob.ellner.motb.91231.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by MAC Supplied By: Barry Glassberg, Transfer by Adam Egert, Mastering by Bill Koucky; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM-700 => Sony TC-D5 >> MAC [4]. Also: Tape flip during Never Trust A Woman patched using gd81-08-28.sbd-patched.painoman source; Crossfades applied for tape flips after Little Red Rooster, Drums, and before U.S. Blues [4]
- **gd1981-08-28.sbd.miller.113680.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> CD [5]. Also: Joe B. Jones assisted with pitch correction for the soundboard recording; Numerous flaws were removed from the recording during the transfer process [5]
- **gd1981-08-28.149185.FOB.Senn.Streeter.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac2496**: taped by Master Cassette Recording by Frank Streeter; transferred by DSD Transfer by Charlie Miller;Edited & reMastered w/ Adobe Audition by Joe Noel; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M) [6]
